learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Exploration progress is not mastery evidence; quiz attempts remain the scored retrieval signal.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Source image + components + infrastructure + distribution → __________

reveal.text: An Image Builder pipeline produces tested AMIs or container images from repeatable recipes.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use to reduce boot-time dependency installation and standardize __________.

reveal.text: Bake dependencies and configuration into repeatable, tested images.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Image Builder creates images; Auto Scaling decides fleet __________.

reveal.text: Use each service for its own role.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Recipe = source + versioned build/test __________.

reveal.text: Recipes define the base image plus components that install/configure/test the image.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Build component vs test component

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: Change recipe/component version → run pipeline → new __________.

reveal.text: Produce a new immutable image version rather than editing an already built image.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Managed registry for container __________.

reveal.text: ECR stores and manages container images for AWS/container workflows.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Image Builder/container pipeline output may be published to a __________.

reveal.text: Use an image registry such as ECR for container image distribution.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: ECR stores images; ECS/EKS __________ them.

reveal.text: Registry and runtime/orchestrator are separate responsibilities.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Template → stack → AWS __________.

reveal.text: A CloudFormation template declares resources; a stack is the deployed instance of that template.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for repeatable, versionable infrastructure __________.

reveal.text: Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible and reviewable.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not rely on manual console changes if the stack should remain __________.

reveal.text: Manual changes can create drift from the declared template.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Define infrastructure in programming languages and synthesize __________.

reveal.text: The AWS CDK defines cloud resources in code and synthesizes CloudFormation templates.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: CDK code → synthesized template → __________.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: CDK does not bypass CloudFormation’s deployment __________.

reveal.text: CDK commonly uses CloudFormation as the deployment engine.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Preview proposed stack __________ before execution.

reveal.text: A change set shows how CloudFormation expects to modify resources.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use before risky production updates to review __________.

reveal.text: Inspect additions, modifications, replacements, and removals before applying.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Change set predicts template-driven changes; it is not drift __________.

reveal.text: Drift detection compares deployed resources with the stack’s expected state.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Find resources whose actual configuration differs from __________.

reveal.text: Drift detection identifies supported resource properties that no longer match the stack definition.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Someone changed a managed resource manually” → __________

reveal.text: Run drift detection and reconcile the resource/template.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Drift detection does not automatically __________ every difference.

reveal.text: It reports drift; remediation is a separate action.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Break reusable infrastructure into parent/child __________.

reveal.text: Nested stacks let templates compose reusable CloudFormation stacks.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for reusable stack components across larger __________.

reveal.text: Useful for modularizing repeated infrastructure patterns.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Nested stacks ≠ StackSets.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Deploy a stack configuration across multiple __________ and Regions.

reveal.text: StackSets centrally deploy stack instances to target AWS accounts and Regions.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for organization-wide baseline resources or repeated multi-account __________.

reveal.text: Common for standardized IAM, logging, configuration, or infrastructure baselines.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Same CloudFormation resources in 50 accounts” → __________

reveal.text: CloudFormation StackSets.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Stack delete can delete resources unless a retention/snapshot __________ says otherwise.

reveal.text: CloudFormation supports deletion/update-replacement policies for resources that need preservation.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Protect persistent data when stacks are replaced/deleted → configure __________.

reveal.text: Use appropriate DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy behavior such as Retain or Snapshot where supported.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Retain means CloudFormation leaves the resource; it does not keep managing it after stack __________.

reveal.text: Understand ownership and lifecycle after retention.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Common failures: IAM permissions, invalid parameters, quota/capacity, subnet IPs, dependency __________.

reveal.text: Read stack events and the underlying service error before retrying blindly.

prompts.label: ⚡ ACTION
prompts.placeholder: CloudFormation failed → inspect stack __________ first.

reveal.text: Stack events show which resource failed and the service error that triggered rollback/failure.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Insufficient free IP addresses in subnet” → fix __________ capacity.

reveal.text: Choose/resize/add subnets or adjust deployment placement so enough addresses are available.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Share supported AWS resources across accounts without duplicating __________.

reveal.text: AWS RAM provides controlled resource sharing across accounts, Organizations, or OUs for supported resource types.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use for centrally owned shared network/resources where supported.

reveal.text: Examples include sharing supported networking and infrastructure resources across accounts.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: RAM shares a resource; StackSets deploy separate __________.

reveal.text: Choose sharing versus replicated deployment based on the architecture.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Code review + history + rollback = infrastructure __________.

reveal.text: Keep infrastructure definitions in version control so changes are auditable and repeatable.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Avoid “works only on one laptop” by pinning versions/state and documenting __________.

reveal.text: Treat deployment tooling and dependencies as part of the reproducible system.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Track who changed infrastructure definition and restore previous version” → __________

reveal.text: Use version control such as Git.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Third-party infrastructure-as-code tool using declarative __________.

reveal.text: Terraform plans and applies infrastructure from configuration while tracking resource state.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Configuration + state → plan → __________

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Terraform is not an AWS-managed CloudFormation __________.

reveal.text: It is a separate IaC ecosystem/tool that can manage AWS resources.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: In-place / rolling / blue-green / canary trade speed, cost, and __________.

reveal.text: Deployment strategy determines how much old/new capacity runs simultaneously and how risk is controlled.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Need quick rollback with parallel old/new environment → __________.

reveal.text: Blue/green is a common clue because traffic can be shifted back.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: No single deployment strategy is best for every workload.

reveal.text: Choose based on downtime tolerance, capacity, validation, and rollback requirements.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A management plane for fleet inventory, configuration, patching, automation, and __________.

reveal.text: Systems Manager provides multiple capabilities for operating managed nodes and AWS resources.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: SSM Agent + IAM/managed-node registration + service permissions → __________.

reveal.text: Managed nodes need the required agent/connectivity/permissions for many Systems Manager capabilities.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Systems Manager is not one feature; choose the specific __________ for the task.

reveal.text: Run Command, Patch Manager, State Manager, Session Manager, Automation, and Maintenance Windows solve different problems.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Execute commands remotely on managed nodes without inbound __________.

reveal.text: Run Command uses Systems Manager to execute documents/commands and report status.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Fleet-wide one-off command or script → __________.

reveal.text: Run Command is a strong fit.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: For a multi-step remediation workflow, Automation may be more __________.

reveal.text: Choose the abstraction that matches the operation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Automate scanning/installing approved operating-system __________.

reveal.text: Patch Manager helps evaluate and install patches according to patch policies/baselines and schedules.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Security patching across managed EC2/on-prem nodes → __________.

reveal.text: Patch Manager is the direct service clue.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Patch Manager does not replace application-specific __________.

reveal.text: OS patching and application deployment are separate concerns.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Maintain a desired node __________ over time.

reveal.text: State Manager associations periodically apply a desired configuration/document to managed nodes.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Ensure a service/configuration remains present on a fleet → __________.

reveal.text: State Manager is designed for recurring desired-state enforcement.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: One-time remote command → use __________ instead.

reveal.text: Run Command is usually the simpler one-off command tool.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Define when disruptive operational tasks may __________.

reveal.text: Maintenance Windows schedule operational tasks against registered targets within controlled windows.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Patch/reboot only Sunday 02:00–04:00 → __________.

reveal.text: Use a Maintenance Window to control timing.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Window + targets + tasks + schedule = controlled __________.

reveal.text: This separates the operational task from the approved execution period.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Interactive shell access without opening inbound SSH/RDP __________.

reveal.text: Session Manager can provide auditable interactive access to managed nodes without traditional inbound administration ports.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Private EC2 administration without bastion/public IP → consider __________.

reveal.text: Session Manager is a strong operational access pattern.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Session Manager access still requires proper IAM and managed-node __________.

reveal.text: No inbound port does not mean no authorization controls.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Multi-step runbooks automate operational __________.

reveal.text: Automation orchestrates AWS API actions, scripts, approvals, and other steps in repeatable runbooks.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Repeatable repair across resources with branching/steps → __________.

reveal.text: Automation is designed for structured operational workflows.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Automation is not only for EC2 shell commands.

reveal.text: Runbooks can orchestrate AWS resource APIs and multiple service actions.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: AWS/SaaS/custom event → EventBridge rule → __________.

reveal.text: Rules route matching events to automation targets.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: React automatically to state changes without polling → __________.

reveal.text: EventBridge is a common event-driven routing layer.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Troubleshoot pattern, bus, target policy, retries, and __________.

reveal.text: Use target metrics/logs and DLQ/retry settings where relevant.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Run custom code in response to events without managing __________.

reveal.text: Lambda provides event-driven compute for short-lived automation and integrations.

prompts.label: ⏱️ WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Custom API logic/remediation that fits function limits → __________.

reveal.text: Lambda is useful when native actions are not enough.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: Do not add Lambda if a direct EventBridge/service target already satisfies the __________.

reveal.text: Prefer simpler native integrations when possible.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Object events can notify supported destinations or integrate with __________.

reveal.text: S3 can publish notifications for selected bucket events to supported targets; S3 events can also flow through EventBridge.

prompts.label: 🔍 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Filter by prefix/suffix to limit which object keys __________.

reveal.text: Notification filters reduce unnecessary downstream work.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: “Run processing when a new object arrives” → __________.

reveal.text: S3 Event Notifications or EventBridge-based S3 events are common answers.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Current SOA-C03 scope includes an AI-assisted operations agent for investigating and resolving __________.

reveal.text: AWS DevOps Agent is included in current exam-guide examples for event-driven operations and remediation.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Agent assistance should still use telemetry, change context, and controlled __________.

reveal.text: Keep remediation auditable and permission-bounded.

prompts.label: 🚫 NOT THIS
prompts.placeholder: It does not replace CloudWatch/EventBridge/Systems Manager as foundational operational __________.

reveal.text: Know how the underlying signals and automation services work.

authoring_notes: Original learning content. Official SOA-C03 exam guide revision 1.1 is the scope authority; the supplied May 2026 study guide was used as a supplementary coverage check and was not copied.
